newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk health minister warns of dangers of kissing.
newsitem.headline: Turk health minister warns of dangers of kissing.

text.p: Turkey's health minister, Yildirim Aktuna, has sent a directive to provincial governors warning of the dangers of people kissing as they greet each other, Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.

"Although it does not have a place in Turkish culture, in recent years the custom of kissing one another while shaking hands has become widespread. As a result of this, bringing under control the diseases contracted in this way has become a problem for health organisations," the directive reads.
Turks of both sexes routinely kiss each other on cheeks when they meet, regardless of sex distinctions, with men kissing other men a common feature of life in Turkey.
The health ministry warning said that kissing could result in viral infections, measles, chicken pox as well as there being a slight risk of contacting AIDS, the agency said.
Aktuna called for reinforcement of the health system to help bring infections spread by kissing under control and a programme of education to teach people of its dangers, Anatolain said.
